text: Charles Boyle, Viscount Dungarvan, 3rd Baron Clifford, FRS (bapt. 12 December 1639 – 12 October 1694), was an English peer and politician belonging to a prominent Anglo-Irish aristocratic family. He was the son of Richard Boyle, 1st Earl of Burlington, and Lady Elizabeth Clifford, 2nd Baroness Clifford suo jure, and held the courtesy title of Viscount Dungarvan from birth. In 1663, he was appointed to the Irish House of Lords as Viscount Dungarvan and became a Fellow of the Royal Society the following year. From 1670 to 1679, he served as Member of Parliament for Tamworth in the British House of Commons, and thereafter represented Yorkshire from 1679 onward. In 1682, he purchased the original Chiswick House, a Jacobean property previously owned by Sir Edward Wardour, which served as a summer retreat for the Boyle family from their central London residence, Burlington House. In 1689, he was elevated to the British House of Lords as Baron Clifford of Lanesborough, a title created for his father in 1644. Upon the death of his mother in 1691, Charles inherited the Barony of Clifford. Although he died in 1694, predeceasing his father, his titles passed to his eldest son, Charles Boyle, who succeeded his grandfather as the 2nd Earl of Burlington. On 7 May 1661, Charles married Lady Jane Seymour (1637–1679), the fourth daughter of William Seymour, 2nd Duke of Somerset, and Lady Frances Devereux; they had five children. After Jane's death in 1679, he married Lady Arethusa Berkeley (1664–1743), daughter of George Berkeley, 1st Earl of Berkeley, and Elizabeth Massingberd, in 1688, and they had one child. Charles Boyle died on 12 October 1694.
